note: Thresholds are provisional (plan § 1). Each control runs with its options as listed and again reversed; a control passes only when every order passes. A same-choice control asks the same state under the question set's own intent wording and under neutral_intent below. c2 fixes c1 per the JL-15 review (N1, N2): every decision-bearing fact (price, stopping time, buff permanence, scrap's sole use, the next tier, what the exit does) is in the option text, so both wordings see the same facts and differ only in framing; the swap also runs on the free-cache state; options within a control are length-matched within 1.25x; the free cache is priced 0 with scrap held, so it cannot read as unaffordable. max_shift is a provisional line beside the same-choice rule: in each order the shift is the largest |P(current) - P(neutral)| over the listed options, and a choice that differs between the wordings fails that order only when the shift exceeds the line. A flip inside the line is a near tie, recorded and not read as a wording effect; the same choice passes at any shift, which is recorded. The line 0.15 is three times the 0.05 order-to-order movement of P(take_cache) under one wording in the c1 live run (0.74 against 0.69, JL-15 review N1), set before any c2 run.
neutral_intent: You control a vehicle in a stage of a video game. Each listed option is an action available right now, with what it involves. Choose the single intent to hold for the next second or two.

controls.rationale: A cache that costs nothing and takes no time to open is a free permanent buff. An instrument that declines it is measuring its own wording. Scrap is held (60) and the price is 0, so the option cannot read as unaffordable.

options.why: You are rolling over the cache now. It opens for 0 scrap and no stop, and its random buff stacks for the rest of the run.
Roll on past the cache to the exit, 200 m ahead, where a 60 s charge clears the stage. The cache stays unopened.
Detour about 2 s onto the scrap line. Scrap is spent only on caches; cache prices rise at the next tier, in 25 s.

controls.rationale: At 8 HP a ram that deals 25 contact damage to the player ends the run. The ram is executable (fast tier), so only judgement keeps it from being chosen.

options.why: Ram the chaser on your line above the fast tier. The contact deals 25 damage to you; 0 health ends the run.
Break off from the chaser and avoid all contact. Health starts to regenerate 5 s after the last hit.
Steer around the chaser and hold the line toward the exit, 160 m ahead, where the exit charge starts.

controls.rationale: A modest cache early in the run with no threats. Every fact the choice rests on is in the options, so the two wordings see the same facts and the choice should not depend on which one asks.

options.why: Stop on the cache for about 1 s and pay 25 of your 140 scrap; its random buff stacks for the rest of the run.
Skip the cache and roll on to the exit, 320 m ahead, where a 60 s charge clears the stage; scrap stays at 140.
Detour about 2 s along the siding for scrap. Scrap is spent only on caches; cache prices rise at tier 2, in 15 s.

controls.rationale: The free-cache state and options under both wordings (JL-15 review N1c). It needs no new prompt text, and it separates a wording effect on a costly cache from one on a free cache.
